name: Scented candles
anchor: route-scoped sovereign inhaled-product content maxima. Lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury read across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division 2022 route table for "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray" (500 / 200 / 200 / 100 ug/kg), corroborated at identical values by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products; total chromium reads across from the Maryland Cannabis Administration inhalation-route value (600 ug/kg) and is published as a screen. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it is a component prohibition on the metal of a wick core and is carried on the scented-candles row as an independent regulatory hard stop, never as a finished-article ceiling. Nickel, tin, aluminium, inorganic arsenic and hexavalent chromium are held under mandatory control because no government sets a content maximum for them in any inhaled consumer product.
native_basis_label: as sold, micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material (the fragrance concentrate, wax, gel, botanical mass or refill charge that is aerosolised, evaporated or combusted), with component-level screening of the article's non-emitting parts; a content screen on the article and its refill, never an emission rate, a per-actuation dose or an indoor-air concentration
scope_note: FORM AND EMISSION MECHANISM. A wick-fed flame burns wax and fragrance at several hundred degrees Celsius. Volatile organics leave in the plume, while non-volatile metals partition between the emitted soot and aerosol and the residual wax, wick ash and vessel film. Combustion concentrates whatever metal the article contained; it does not destroy it. SCOPE. In scope: wick-bearing scented candles in every presentation, including filled glass and ceramic jars, tins, pillars, votives, tapers, tealights and multi-wick vessels, together with the vessel, wick and any decoration supplied as part of the article. Out of scope: unscented candles marketed solely for illumination or ritual with no fragrance claim (assessed case-by-case on the residual row where an air-emission claim is made), oil lamps and liquid-paraffin lamps, and the electric or tealight warmers used with wax melts, which are appliances rather than emitting products. COMPONENTS SAMPLED. The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm, beeswax or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any mineral or polymer hardener, opacifier or UV stabiliser; the wick, its core, sustainer tab and adhesive; the glass, ceramic, tinplate or aluminium vessel and any glaze, enamel, lustre, decal or metallic surface coating; and the lid. BASIS, AND WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT MEASURE. The panel is a CONTENT SCREEN on the article and on its refill, expressed in micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material. It is not an inhalation exposure limit, not an emission-rate limit, not a per-actuation or per-hour dose limit, and not an indoor-air concentration limit, and it must not be presented as any of those. No credible sovereign government sets an inhalation exposure limit for these metals in a consumer air product, and HMTc does not manufacture one: no occupational exposure limit and no ambient- or indoor-air guideline is converted into a product ceiling anywhere in this category. Because this is a combustion form, the content screen is a LOWER BOUND on what the emission path can carry: burning removes volatile mass and leaves the non-volatile metal partitioned between the emitted soot and aerosol and the residual wax, wick and ash, so post-burn residue and ash analysis is mandatory alongside the unburnt article. ROUTING. Placement in this category follows the taxonomy boundary rules: the primary exposure pathway must be inhalation or ambient-air emission; an essential oil sold as aromatherapy for diffusion routes here, the same oil sold as a topical leave-on skin product routes to Category 13 and sold as a dietary supplement routes to Category 16; and marketing and positioning decide routing where one formulation could serve several functions.
basis_guard_note: Category 22 numeric cells are anchored ONLY in route-scoped inhaled-product content instruments, whose register basis strings are "product as tested" (Colorado, Maryland) and "cannabis or cannabis product" (California). The guard admits exactly those and rejects, by construction, every other basis family the register carries: dietary wet-weight maximum levels (an ingestion basis), food-contact and toy element-migration limits (a leachate basis), RoHS and REACH percent-by-weight restrictions on homogeneous materials, plastics, paints and batteries (an end-of-life materials basis), surface-coating dried-film limits, drinking-water statutory limits (a per-litre basis), cosmetic technically-avoidable trace limits (a dermal basis), colour-additive purity specifications, feed 12-percent-moisture bases, and the candlewick prohibition threshold, which is expressed on the mass of the metal in the wick core and not on any product. A number in the wrong basis is not a maximum level for this product form and must never anchor a row here.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial setting: the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form in its native basis; disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; control where neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.binding_control: INDEPENDENT REGULATORY HARD STOP, additional to the published ceiling and not a substitute for it. 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) declares candles with lead-cored wicks, and such wicks in themselves, to be banned hazardous substances in the United States, using 0.06 percent lead by weight of the metal in the wick core as the definitional threshold (register row us_16cfr1500_17a13_pb_lead_cored_candle_wicks_600ppm, 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal). Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 mirror the prohibition for candles with lead-containing wicks and for candle wicks themselves. That threshold is measured on the metal of the wick core, in a basis that is not this row's basis, and it is NOT published as this row's lead ceiling: doing so would put a 600,000 ug/kg number on a scented candle and would misrepresent a prohibition as a permission. It is enforced instead as a pass/fail component test. Every metal-cored wick is sampled separately, the core metal is digested and analysed for lead by ICP-MS, and any core exceeding 0.06 percent lead by weight of the metal is a banned hazardous substance in the United States and a prohibited import in Australia. That finding blocks certification outright, irrespective of the article's bulk lead content and irrespective of the 500 ug/kg ceiling.
Pb.basis: as sold, ug of element per kg of the emitting material (product as tested)
Pb.source_scope: inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray
Pb.label: read-across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division route-scoped maximum for inhaled product and metered-dose nasal spray (500 ug/kg), corroborated at the identical value by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products
Pb.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a lead content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 500 ug/kg, from Colorado (co2022 inhaled/nasal row). California DCC section 15723 independently sets the identical 0.5 ug/g for inhalable products (us_ca_dcc_2026_pb_inhalable_cannabis_0_5ugg), so two sub-national regulators converge on this value. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: Maryland inhalation route 1000 ug/kg, Massachusetts all-uses protocol 500 ug/kg (equal but route-unspecific), Nevada 1200 ug/kg, Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 5000 ug/kg. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the unburnt wax-and-fragrance body, sampled through its full depth by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. Post-burn residue and ash are analysed in addition to the unburnt article, because combustion removes volatile mass and concentrates non-volatile metal in what is left and in what is emitted.

iAs.rationale: No government sets an inorganic-arsenic content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. Every route-scoped inhaled-product instrument regulates arsenic as the unspeciated total: Colorado, California, Maryland, Massachusetts, Nevada and Israel all publish total arsenic and none of them speciates, so there is no inorganic-arsenic cell anywhere to read across from. The article and component instruments checked were EU RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU Annex II (lead, cadmium, total mercury and hexavalent chromium in the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment), the EU Batteries Regulation Annex I (mercury, cadmium and lead in batteries), REACH Annex XVII entry 23 (cadmium in synthetic polymers, paint and painted articles), REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin expressed as tin in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public), REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and hexavalent chromium in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles), REACH Annex XVII entry 63 paragraph 7 (lead in mouthable articles), Canada SOR/2016-193 (lead and mercury in surface coating materials), Canada SOR/2018-83 (lead in accessible parts of children's products), Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892 (lead and cadmium in listed covered consumer products), and the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 with EN 71-3 (element migration from toy materials). Every one of them governs a component of an article in a different basis, and none of them is a content maximum for the material a home-air product puts into the breathing zone. The cosmetic content instruments checked and rejected on route were Germany BVL 2017 (technically avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics), Health Canada's cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits, the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive contaminant guideline v3 (2019), Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9, China's 2015 Cosmetics Safety and Technical Standards, India's Cosmetics Rules 2020, Indonesia BPOM 16/2024, Malaysia NPRA, the New Zealand Cosmetic Products Group Standard, Kenya KS 2937:2021, Taiwan's 2024 prohibited-ingredient residual limits, EAEU TR CU 009/2011, and the Hong Kong Mercury Control Ordinance cosmetics provision. All of them are content limits for products applied to the human body on a dermal or mucosal basis. A home-air product is not applied to the body, so none of them is route-applicable. A NOT-MATERIAL determination is deliberately rejected rather than adopted for convenience, because inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction and it is genuinely material in this row. Inorganic arsenic is material here through mineral pigments, glaze frits and lustres on the vessel, and through arsenic in mineral wax fillers; arsenic in these sources is predominantly inorganic. The cell is therefore a control: testing is mandatory, the species is bounded by identity below the published total-arsenic ceiling of 200 ug/kg, and no number is invented. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
iAs.reference_method: Total arsenic on every certified lot of the unburnt wax-and-fragrance body, sampled through its full depth by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the ArCl interference. Reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS is ordered whenever the total-arsenic screen reaches half the published total-arsenic ceiling (100 ug/kg), and unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier of mineral filler, pigment, glaze, frit, clay, charcoal, joss powder, hydrocolloid or dried botanical material. Component-level sampling covers the wax base (paraffin, soy, coconut, palm, beeswax or a blend); the fragrance load; the dye or pigment; any mineral or polymer hardener, opacifier or UV stabiliser; the wick, its core, sustainer tab and adhesive; the glass, ceramic, tinplate or aluminium vessel and any glaze, enamel, lustre, decal or metallic surface coating; and the lid. Post-burn residue and ash from a controlled test burn are digested and analysed in addition to the unburnt article, because combustion concentrates non-volatile metal rather than destroying it. Because inorganic arsenic is a fraction of total arsenic, a lot in which inorganic arsenic alone reaches 200 ug/kg also fails the published total-arsenic ceiling. No fixed numeric ceiling is published, because no sovereign government sets one for this analyte in any inhaled or home-air product, and a ceiling is not invented. Every result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule: the lot is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the wax supplier, fragrance house, dye or pigment supplier, wick supplier and vessel or decorator supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. This row's emitting material is a manufactured non-marine formulation (the unburnt wax-and-fragrance body, sampled through its full depth) with no methylation pathway, no aquatic trophic transfer and no marine-derived or wild-harvested animal input, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so MeHg is less than or equal to tHg by identity and is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury ceiling of 100 ug/kg. Methylmercury is additionally thermally labile and decomposes well below the temperatures reached in any heated or combustion form in this category, so no thermal pathway creates it either. No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury limit for any air-care product, and no routed occurrence source reports methylmercury in one, which is the speciation-aware condition the not-material integrity gate applies. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling.
MeHg.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell, which is determined on every lot by EPA 7473 thermal decomposition/amalgamation atomic absorption or by ICP-MS after closed-vessel digestion. Methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total mercury reaches half the published total-mercury ceiling (50 ug/kg), or where a reformulation introduces any marine-derived, fish-derived or wild-harvested animal raw material, which would additionally require the row to be re-dispositioned from not-material to control.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury content limit for an air freshener, evaporator, puff releaser, candle, wax melt, diffuser, incense, potpourri, vacuum fragrance additive or fragrance refill. Every methylmercury instrument on the register is scoped exclusively to fish, crustaceans, molluscs and other aquatic animals (Hong Kong Cap. 132V, EU Regulation (EU) 2022/617, US FDA CPG 540.600, FSANZ Schedule 19, Thailand MOPH 414, Vietnam QCVN 8-2, Philippines PNS/BAFS 194, Mexico NOM-242, GSO 193, Trinidad and Tobago). Methylmercury is a species of, and arithmetically cannot exceed, total mercury, which this row publishes at 100 ug/kg by disclosed read-across from the Colorado inhalation-route maximum.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: Route-scoped inhaled-product instruments: Colorado MED 2022, California DCC section 15723, Maryland Cannabis Administration Rev. 6.0, Massachusetts CCC 2020, Nevada CCB 2020, Israel MoH IMC-GMP 152 - none publishes methylmercury. Article and component instruments: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU, EU Batteries Regulation Annex I, REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23, 63 and 72, Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2018-83, Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892, EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, US 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) - none publishes methylmercury. Cosmetic instruments: Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, ASEAN Cosmetic Directive v3 2019, Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9, China CSAR 2015, India Cosmetics Rules 2020, Indonesia BPOM 16/2024, Malaysia NPRA, New Zealand Group Standard, Kenya KS 2937:2021, Taiwan 2024, EAEU TR CU 009/2011, Hong Kong Mercury Control Ordinance - all regulate total mercury only. Dietary methylmercury instruments are fish-scoped and excluded by applicability.

Ni.rationale: No government sets a nickel content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. Every route-scoped inhaled-product instrument on the register omits nickel entirely, including Maryland's inhalation-route table, which publishes lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium and total chromium but no nickel. The nearest nickel instruments were checked and each fails on basis or on route: the EU Toy Safety Directive nickel values are element MIGRATION limits from toy material under EN 71-3, not content limits; REACH Annex XVII entry 27 governs nickel RELEASE RATE from skin-piercing and prolonged-skin-contact articles; Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9 set nickel content limits for cosmetics on a dermal basis; and EU Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 sets dietary nickel maximum levels on an ingestion basis. No conversion between a migration limit, a release rate, a dermal cosmetic limit and a total-content limit for an inhaled product is defensible, and none is performed. A not-material determination is rejected: Nickel is material here: metal wick cores and sustainer tabs, nickel-bearing pigments, and the fact that this category's own contamination-platform description identifies nickel as one of the two dirty-platform metals for combustion emitters, because metal-bearing colorants and fragrance carriers volatilise into the breathing zone at flame temperature. The cell is a control. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.

Post-burn residue and ash from a controlled test burn are digested and analysed in addition to the unburnt article, because combustion concentrates non-volatile metal rather than destroying it. Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is not the health-relevant analyte. It is dominated by trivalent chromium, an essential trace element, while the species of concern by the inhalation route is hexavalent chromium, a Group 1 respiratory carcinogen. The Maryland inhalation-route value is a real sovereign number in the right basis and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is the tripwire that triggers hexavalent-chromium speciation (see the Cr-VI cell), not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count. Total chromium is never satisfied by a hexavalent-chromium result and hexavalent chromium is never satisfied by a total-chromium result.
Cr.basis: as sold, ug of element per kg of the emitting material (product as tested)
Cr.source_scope: usable cannabis and cannabis products except edible products; inhalation route
Cr.label: read-across from the Maryland Cannabis Administration inhalation-route total-chromium maximum (600 ug/kg), published as a SCREEN
Cr.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a total chromium content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 600 ug/kg, from Maryland (inhalation route). Maryland is the only regulator on the register that publishes a chromium value scoped to the inhalation route. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: no other jurisdiction on the register publishes a chromium value for any inhaled product: California DCC section 15723, the Colorado route table, the Massachusetts protocol, the Nevada action levels and Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 all omit chromium entirely. Maryland's own oral-route and cutaneous-route chromium values for the same products, 1,100,000 ug/kg, are a different route scope and are deliberately not used. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the unburnt wax-and-fragrance body, sampled through its full depth by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. Post-burn residue and ash are analysed in addition to the unburnt article, because combustion removes volatile mass and concentrates non-volatile metal in what is left and in what is emitted.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel screen number in this programme; it is the toxic species reached by reflex speciation from total chromium. No government sets a hexavalent-chromium content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product: Maryland publishes plain total chromium for the inhalation route and does not speciate, and no other route-scoped instrument publishes chromium in any form. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other. A not-material determination is rejected: Chromium is material here and specifically so for a combustion form: chromium in wick supports, chrome-bearing pigments, mordants and glaze frits can be oxidised from the trivalent to the hexavalent state at flame and glow temperatures, and inhaled hexavalent chromium is a Group 1 respiratory carcinogen. The cell is a control with reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium on every certified lot of the unburnt wax-and-fragrance body, sampled through its full depth by digestion and ICP-MS, read against the published total-chromium SCREEN of 600 ug/kg.
